view.stem: At the specified temperature and with the specified surface conditions, molten tin wets copper, silver, and brass, but does not wet stainless steel, aluminum, or chromium. Which conclusions about joining these metals with tin are justified by these facts? Select all justified statements. Discuss the model only; no actual soldering is required.

options.text: For copper, wetting supports the tin-surface contact condition needed for soldering; this fact alone does not establish that a usable joint will form.
For silver, tin wetting by itself guarantees a strong joint, regardless of all other joining conditions.
Because tin does not wet chromium in the stated conditions, chromium can never be joined with tin under any other temperature or surface treatment.
Chromium, stainless steel, and aluminum fail the needed wetting/contact condition in this model. This does not establish impossibility under every possible surface treatment.
Tin wetting brass establishes that any two metallic surfaces can form a joint with tin, so the stated nonwetting exclusions do not matter.
Copper, silver, and brass meet the wetting prerequisite under the given conditions. This identifies the qualifying set, but establishes neither joint strength nor success under different conditions.

intent.task: Infer the complete qualifying wetting set and distinguish a necessary contact condition from a guarantee of joining success or an all-condition material claim.
intent.source_solution: Under the given wetting classification, copper, silver, and brass meet the wetting prerequisite; chromium, stainless steel, and aluminum do not. Wetting supports the required tin-surface contact but does not establish all other requirements for a usable joint. The specified surface and temperature conditions cannot establish either guaranteed success or permanent impossibility under different treatments. Therefore a, d, and f are justified. Wet and nonwet metal names occur in both justified and unjustified conclusions, so affirmative-list copying does not determine the complete true set.
intent.unit_reason: One native multiple response evaluates a related set of physical implications and the complete material classification. Correct conclusions include both the wet and the nonwet groups; incorrect conclusions include unsupported implications about each group.
limitations: The result establishes only the necessary wetting condition under the given surface conditions; it does not prove successful real soldering or practical skill.
Recognizing supplied implications does not demonstrate independently constructing an explanation of wetting or performing a materials experiment.

rationales.derivation: Copper is in the stated wetting group. The wetting/contact prerequisite is satisfied, but a necessary condition alone does not establish the existence or strength of a usable joint.
Silver meets the wetting prerequisite, not every requirement for joint formation and strength. The conclusion asserts a sufficient all-condition guarantee that the wetting data do not supply.
rationales.misconception: Replace the necessary wetting condition with a sufficient guarantee of joint strength and ignore other joining conditions.

rationales.derivation: The given nonwetting property applies to the specified surface and temperature conditions. It does not establish the same property under every other surface treatment or temperature, so permanent impossibility does not follow.
rationales.misconception: Generalize a conditional nonwetting fact to every possible surface treatment and temperature.

rationales.derivation: All three named metals are in the stated nonwetting group and therefore fail this contact prerequisite in the model. The statement explicitly limits that exclusion rather than inferring all-condition impossibility.
The datum concerns wetting of brass in the specified conditions. It neither proves joining for every pair of metals nor cancels the explicit nonwetting exclusions.
rationales.misconception: Transfer one metal's stated wetting behavior to all metallic surfaces and discard the excluded group.

rationales.derivation: The three wet metals form the complete qualifying set for the specified prerequisite. Identifying this set is distinct from proving joint strength or transferring the result to different conditions.
